<!--
WHEN THIS TEMPLATE IS USED
The product was prototyped (or built) before the bet was written down. This
template turns what the prototype proved into the same product brief `/brainstorm`
writes, so downstream skills (`/prd-review`, `/map-features`, `/gate-check
definition`) can read it like any other brief. It carries the thirteen product-brief
headings of `.claude/docs/templates/product-brief.md` in the same order, plus
`## Prototype Evidence` at the end.

Written by `/reverse-document brief <path>` to `design/product/product-brief.md` when
no brief exists yet. It never overwrites an existing brief without an explicit "May I
overwrite …?"; when one exists it writes
`design/product/product-brief-from-code-YYYY-MM-DD.md` by default, for the user to
merge. `/prototype` points here when a concept proves out (verdict PROCEED)
and no brief exists yet.

RULES FOR REVERSE-DOCUMENTING
- Separate what the prototype **showed** (observed in sessions, measured, in the
  code) from what the team **intends** (not yet tested). Label intentions
  `Hypothesis:`.
- A section the prototype and the user cannot answer is written
  `NOT DETERMINED — <what would answer it>` — never filled with a plausible guess.
  Such a section is a gap for `/prd-review` to flag, not a pass.
- Every claim about users cites the prototype report, a usability report or an
  interview by participant ID.
- The optional `## Brand Direction Anchor` follows the same rule as in the product
  brief: omit it (heading included) when there is no UI surface or brand direction
  is deferred to `/design-language`. A prototype's visual styling is not a brand
  direction.

MACHINE CONTRACT — keep every `##` heading exactly as spelled, in this order.
Examples use Moa, a B2C subscription savings app for the Korean market.
Delete these comments when the brief is written.
-->

## Elevator Pitch

> [One or two sentences, restated from what the prototype turned out to be — which
> may differ from what it set out to be.]

## Problem Statement

[The problem the prototype addressed, with the evidence the sessions produced.
Where the prototype only assumed the problem, say so and mark it `Hypothesis:`.]

## Target Users & Jobs-to-be-Done

[The segment the prototype was tested with (from the report's participants), the
jobs observed, and whether participants matched the intended segment. List jobs
the prototype did not test separately as hypotheses.]

## Alternatives & Positioning

[What participants compared the prototype to, unprompted, and what they use today.
Add researched alternatives with sources; mark unresearched ones
`NOT DETERMINED — competitor scan not done`.]

## Value Proposition

[The value participants actually experienced — the success moment observed — and
the value still hypothetical.]

## Business Model Hypothesis

[Usually untested by a prototype. Record any price or willingness-to-pay signal the
sessions or a fake door produced; everything else is `Hypothesis:` or
`NOT DETERMINED`.]

## Product Principles & Anti-Goals

[Principles the prototype's best and worst moments suggest, each with a decision
test. Mark them draft: they have not been stress-tested (PD-PRINCIPLES runs when
`/brainstorm` revises the brief).]

## Brand Direction Anchor

<!-- OPTIONAL — see the rule in the comment at the top. -->

[Only if the team has chosen a brand direction; otherwise delete this section.]

## Success Metrics

[North Star and at least one guardrail. Use the prototype's measures as baselines
where they exist; label them directional when the sample was small.]

## Riskiest Assumptions

| # | Assumption | Risk | Test | Result | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [the assumption the prototype tested] | [Value / Usability / Feasibility / Viability] | [the prototype — `prototypes/<name>-concept/REPORT.md`] | [what happened] | [Validated / Invalidated] |
| 2 | [an assumption the prototype did not touch] | [...] | [proposed test] | — | Untested |

## MVP Scope

[What the prototype showed must be in the MVP, and what the team adds. Remember the
prototype code is throwaway: MVP capabilities are built from scratch in the code
roots.]

## Non-Goals

[What the prototype deliberately skipped that stays out of the MVP, and what
participants asked for that the team decides not to build now.]

## Open Questions

[Questions the prototype raised — confusion points, feasibility unknowns, pricing —
each with an owner and how it will be answered.]

## Prototype Evidence

| Prototype | Path | Verdict | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| [name] | [clickable / code / fake-door / concierge] | [PROCEED / PIVOT / KILL] | `prototypes/[name]-concept/REPORT.md` |

- **Key measures**: [task success, conversion, continuation — with n]
- **What carried over**: [confirmed assumptions, numbers, copy or flows that worked]
- **What did not**: [refuted assumptions and the pivots taken; link `PIVOT-NOTE.md`
  files]
- **Spikes**: [`prototypes/<name>-spike-YYYY-MM-DD/SPIKE-NOTE.md` results that bear
  on feasibility]
- **Limits of this evidence**: [sample size, segment fit, what the paths used cannot
  show]
